headline: Ward 39 has libraries and houses of worship, but few places to meet someone new.
summary:
Ward 39's best and worst numbers split by audience. The ward has the second-most libraries of any in Chicago and one of the widest ranges of religious traditions among its houses of worship, both places built for people who already belong to a congregation or hold a library card. What's scarce is the kind of place built for meeting someone new. Licensed music and dance venues here rank near the bottom of the city, and a modeled estimate puts the share of residents seeing friends weekly among the lowest as well. The ward is well stocked with institutions and short on rooms to mingle in.

A second pattern runs through the ward's better numbers. The office itself performs well by the measures that track it directly. The alder's attendance record for the current council session ranks third of 50, and the ward drew the third-highest share of any aldermanic menu budget for park spending, both facts about the office rather than the block. Building permits also clear here in under a week on average, fourth-fastest among the 47 wards this measure covers, which is a genuine service number rather than a spending choice. None of that connects to the loudest weak spot on the page. More than half the ward's park drinking fountains, 54.6 percent, carry a history of elevated lead readings, a 47th-of-50 finish with no caveat attached in the underlying data.
reading_the_rankings: Two of this ward's worst-looking numbers are less alarming once you look at how they're built. Per-pupil school spending here lands dead last of 50 wards, but the figure is enrollment-weighted, so the ward's largest schools set most of the average and a handful of big buildings can carry the whole number. It describes the schools serving this ward rather than a budget decision anyone made about the ward. The graffiti removal ranking works the same way from the other side. Ward 39 finishes 49th of 50 for how many days it takes to close a graffiti request, which sounds like a long wait, but the raw figure is well under a single day. Finishing last here still means an answer inside a day, just slower than an unusually fast citywide field.

news.headline: Art Institute's 'Project Windows' Gets Boost From NW Side Businesses
news.note: Six spots across the ward, including Superdawg and the Edgebrook branch library, are displaying local artwork this summer as part of the Art Institute's annual Project Windows program.

news.headline: Police SWAT Team Officer, Woman Shot In Albany Park: 'Absolutely Tragic'
news.note: A police SWAT officer and a 67-year-old woman were shot during a domestic incident and hostage situation in Albany Park, and a suspect was later taken into custody.

news.headline: Protesters Want ICE Out After Chaotic Albany Park Arrest: 'Midway Blitz Is Over, But ICE Has Not Left'
news.note: About 150 people rallied in Horner Park after federal immigration agents made a chaotic arrest at Lawrence and Kedzie in Albany Park.
